__inputs.name: DS_CLOUDWATCH
__inputs.label: CloudWatch
__inputs.description: CloudWatch with read access to AWS/RDS metrics

title: SQL Server on Amazon RDS — mssql-exporter + CloudWatch
description: Engine metrics from mssql-exporter (Prometheus) next to host metrics from CloudWatch (AWS/RDS). Set instance_label to the RDS DB instance identifier so both selectors use the same name.

list.name: sqlserver_instance
list.label: sqlserver_instance (exporter)
list.description: With instance_label set to the RDS DB instance identifier this matches the RDS instance selector.

panels.title: SQL Server
panels.description: sqlserver_up from the exporter: 1 when the exporter can reach SQL Server.

panels.title: Current host
panels.description: @@SERVERNAME of the instance answering on the endpoint. On RDS it changes on stop/start and Multi-AZ failover; set instance_label to keep the sqlserver_instance label stable.

panels.title: Oldest last FULL backup
panels.description: Age of the oldest 'last FULL backup' across databases. On RDS, automated backups show up as daily snapshot FULL backups.

panels.title: CPU utilization & CPU credits
panels.description: CPU credits only exist on burstable classes (db.t3/db.t4g).

panels.title: Freeable memory
panels.description: SQL Server reserves most of the memory for its buffer pool, so low freeable memory is normal; compare with page life expectancy below. CloudWatch does not publish SwapUsage for SQL Server.

panels.title: Disk writes (CloudWatch) vs SQL Server file writes (exporter)
panels.description: The volume also absorbs writes SQL Server files do not account for (RDS backups, agents), so the CloudWatch line is usually higher.

panels.title: Top waits (ms/s)
panels.description: Wait time accumulated per second by wait type (sys.dm_os_wait_stats). Idle/background waits (lazy writer, checkpoint, queue and timer waits, HADR housekeeping) are excluded here; HADR_SYNC_COMMIT and other waits that slow queries are kept.

panels.title: Top queries (by CPU)
panels.description: Requires the top_queries collector (and include_text for the statement).

defaults.noValue: top_queries collector disabled or no data

panels.title: Index fragmentation (most fragmented)
panels.description: Requires the index_fragmentation collector. On RDS, create a user for the exporter login in each database to read (CONNECT ANY DATABASE cannot be granted).

defaults.noValue: index_fragmentation collector disabled or not collected yet

panels.title: Time since last backup
panels.description: RDS automated backups: daily snapshot FULL backups and LOG backups every 5 minutes. Native backups (rds_backup_database) show up as FULL/DIFFERENTIAL with their real duration.

panels.title: Log used (%) by database
panels.description: On RDS the Percent Log Used counter has no instance for master, model, msdb and rdsadmin (HML-026); user databases are reported.
Multi-AZ on RDS SQL Server Standard uses Basic Availability Groups: one AG per database (GUID name) plus RDSAG0 for rdsadmin. Empty on Single-AZ.
panels.title: Multi-AZ (Always On) replicas

panels.description: Per database replica: synchronization state, suspension, lag and queues. Queues are absent while data movement is suspended (SQL Server reports NULL). Aggregated across every exporter in the AG (a secondary only sees its own replica), so the instance selector does not apply here.
panels.title: Multi-AZ (Always On) databases
